correctness.rationale: Every regular nilpotent target lies in the GL_n(q)-orbit of J_n; its invertible polynomial centralizer has q^(n-1)(q-1) elements and orbit size L=∏_{i=0}^{n-2}(q^n−q^i). For AB=J_n, A has either rank n (GL_n choices, unique B) or rank n−1, with image im J_n (L surjections and q^n choices of B). Thus each fiber is q^(n-1)(2q−1)L and the exact pair count is its product by L. Dividing by the established nilpotent-product count q^(2n²)(2q^(-n)−q^(-2n)) yields the claimed conditional product expression. The n→∞ positive Euler product and q→∞ uniform O(q^-2) follow from the absolutely summable tail. Independently enumerated all ordered pairs for (q,n)=(2,2),(3,2),(2,3), with regular counts 54,960,21168. Extension-field q=4 enumeration was inspected in source and saved log but not independently repeated.
residual_risks: Enumeration corroborates small fields/dimensions; the proof is the rank-orbit calculation.

This is not merely recomputing the nilpotent union event.
